title: ONNX-EdgeIDS: A Lightweight Two-Stage Edge Serving Toolkit for Network Intrusion Detection
description:
ONNX-EdgeIDS is research software for deploying machine-learning network intrusion detection on resource-constrained edge devices. It provides Kafka and ZeroMQ replay for CICIDS2017-derived flow records, a first-stage anomaly gate that filters high-volume traffic, and a second-stage tree-ensemble classifier served by ONNX Runtime or by a dependency-minimal NumPy engine exported from the same ONNX graph, together with a release gate that checks the two runtimes agree before deployment.

This release changes the gate's default boundary probes to two per split node on the exact float32 crossing of the split: the last raw value ONNX Runtime's float32 scaler sends to the true branch, and its successor. That pair catches, at every node it reaches, any fault that keeps the node's decision a monotone threshold on its own feature (float64 arithmetic, a reordered scaler, rounded thresholds, an exchanged comparison), which the earlier placement on the threshold and one float32 step either side does not guarantee where the scale is below one; it also needs a third fewer probes. The earlier placement remains available with --probe-set three. The research/ directory carries the experiment code and result files behind the accompanying papers, including the probe-completeness analysis and a comparison with fuzzing and mutation-testing baselines.
